items.title: Smoothness of a relative global complete intersection is detected by a nonvanishing maximal minor
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a relative global complete intersection S = R[x_1, ..., x_n]/(f_1, ..., f_c) the lemma characterises smoothness at a prime by the existence of a c-element subset of the variables whose Jacobian minor does not vanish at that prime (statement lines 37845-37857). The proof does not compute the differential module directly: it identifies the naive cotangent complex of the presentation with the two-term complex given by the Jacobian, notes that the maximal minors are the displayed polynomials, and then reads smoothness from whether the localized complex becomes a free module of rank n - c, in both directions (proof lines 37859-37887). Relating a nonvanishing minor to the rank of the localized complex is the content. H2.
